intro: Welcome back! You know the past simple, the past continuous and the past perfect. Now you'll put them together to tell a real story: set the scene, say what happened in order, add your feelings, and react when a friend tells you a story. Warm-up: think of a funny, scary or embarrassing moment that happened to you.
teachingNotes: This is a speaking lesson that puts together grammar the learner already has: the past simple (a2-past-simple-regular/irregular), the past continuous with when/while (b1-past-continuous), the past perfect (b1-past-perfect) and the order words first/then/next/after that/finally/before/after/when/so (a2-linkers-sequence). Recap in a line, don't re-teach the forms. Teach the shape of a story: 1) set the scene (when, where, who, and what was happening), 2) what happened (the events in order), 3) how it ended and how you felt. Good contexts: mudik, a KRL ride, an ojek, a wedding, a problem at work.

Narrative tenses: the past continuous (was/were + -ing) is the background (It was raining, everyone was waiting for the KRL); the past simple is the main line of events, in order (The train came. We got on.); the past perfect (had + third form) goes BACK to something that happened earlier (I couldn't pay because I had left my wallet at home). The node's common error is the Indonesian trap of no tense marking: Indonesian verbs don't change, the time word does the work (Kemarin saya pergi ke pantai dan saya lihat penyu), so learners say *'Yesterday I go to the beach and I see a turtle' → 'Yesterday I went to the beach and I saw a turtle.' Check EVERY verb, especially the second and third after 'and'. Two other slips: a story with every verb in -ing (a scene with no events), and 'had' for a single event (*'Last week I had gone to Bogor' → 'went').

Story linkers: first, then, next, after that (from A2); suddenly (tiba-tiba) for a quick, unexpected event that cuts into the background; finally for the last event or the end of a long wait; in the end (akhirnya, pada akhirnya) for the final result after problems or changes; at the end of + a noun (di akhir): at the end of the film / the day / the month. Error: *'in the end of the film' → 'at the end of the film'. 'At the end' alone, when it's clear what ended (Everyone clapped at the end), is also correct: accept it, but test only 'at the end of + noun' vs 'in the end'. Finally and in the end often both fit: never make them an either-or question. Indonesian 'akhirnya' as a RESULT is 'so' (A2): Hujan, akhirnya kami di rumah → It rained, so we stayed home.

Details and feelings: add who, where and what you saw or heard (the KRL was packed, 500 guests), and feelings inside the story: I couldn't believe it! It was so embarrassing / scary / funny. I was so embarrassed / scared. We laughed so much. ('so' here = very, as in A2 'so hot'.) -ing describes the situation (embarrassing = memalukan), -ed describes how a person feels (embarrassed = malu): *'I was so embarrassing' is wrong (it means you made other people feel bad). Same for boring/bored, tiring/tired, surprising/surprised; scary/scared is the irregular pair. Luckily (= fortunately, untungnya) before a good turn, Unfortunately (sayangnya) before a bad one.

Listener reactions: surprise → Really? / No way! / Seriously? (masa sih? / yang bener!); asking for more → What happened next? / And then what? / How did that happen? (kok bisa?); bad news → Oh no! / That's terrible! / Poor you! (kasihan: not *'Pity you'); funny or embarrassing → How embarrassing! / That's so funny!; a good ending → Thank goodness! / Lucky you! The reaction must match the mood of the story (not 'That's great!' to bad news). 'No way!' here is friendly surprise, not 'tidak mau'. Treat How + adjective! (How embarrassing!) and I couldn't believe it! as phrases to remember.

Limits: no past perfect continuous (had been + -ing), no used to / would for past habits, no reported speech (tell what people said with direct speech: He said, 'Sorry!'), no third conditional, no passive. When the learner tells a story, praise the shape first, then correct ONE thing (usually a verb left in the present).

keyPoints.title: Tell it in order: scene, events, ending
keyPoints.explanation: A good story has three parts. Set the scene: when, where, who, and what was happening. Then tell what happened, in order, with first, then, after that and suddenly (something quick and unexpected). End with how it ended and how you felt: finally, in the end (= the final result, akhirnya). at the end of + a noun = di akhir: at the end of the film. Not 'in the end of'.

examples.en: It was the day before Lebaran, and we were driving to Solo.
examples.id: Waktu itu sehari sebelum Lebaran, dan kami sedang menyetir ke Solo.

examples.en: Suddenly our car made a strange noise and stopped.
examples.id: Tiba-tiba mobil kami mengeluarkan suara aneh lalu berhenti.

examples.en: In the end, we got to my grandmother's house at midnight.
examples.id: Akhirnya, kami sampai di rumah nenek tengah malam.

id.title: Ceritakan berurutan: latar, kejadian, akhir
id.explanation: Cerita yang bagus punya tiga bagian. Bangun latarnya: kapan, di mana, siapa, dan apa yang sedang terjadi. Lalu ceritakan apa yang terjadi, berurutan, dengan first, then, after that dan suddenly (sesuatu yang cepat dan tidak terduga). Tutup dengan bagaimana akhirnya dan apa yang kamu rasakan: finally, in the end (= hasil akhirnya, akhirnya). at the end of + kata benda = di akhir: at the end of the film. Bukan 'in the end of'.

keyPoints.title: Add details, feelings and reactions
keyPoints.explanation: Add details (who, where, what you saw) and say how you felt: I couldn't believe it! It was so embarrassing. Luckily … before something good, Unfortunately … before something bad. embarrassing / scary = the situation; embarrassed / scared = how you felt (not 'I was so embarrassing'). When you listen to a story, react: Really? No way! What happened next? Oh no!

examples.en: Everyone was looking at me. It was so embarrassing!
examples.id: Semua orang melihat ke arahku. Malu banget!

examples.en: Luckily, a mechanic came and fixed the car.
examples.id: Untungnya, seorang montir datang dan memperbaiki mobilnya.

id.title: Tambahkan detail, perasaan dan reaksi
id.explanation: Tambahkan detail (siapa, di mana, apa yang kamu lihat) dan katakan apa yang kamu rasakan: I couldn't believe it! It was so embarrassing. Luckily … sebelum hal yang baik, Unfortunately … sebelum hal yang buruk. embarrassing / scary = situasinya; embarrassed / scared = perasaanmu (bukan 'I was so embarrassing'). Saat mendengarkan cerita, beri reaksi: Really? No way! What happened next? Oh no!

keyPoints.title: Three past tenses in one story
keyPoints.explanation: The past continuous (was/were + -ing) is the background: what was already happening. The past simple tells the events, in order. The past perfect (had + third form) goes back to something that happened earlier. Indonesian verbs don't change, but in English every verb in a past story is in a past form: Yesterday I went to the beach and I saw a turtle (not 'I go … I see').

examples.en: It was raining, and everyone was waiting for the KRL.
examples.id: Waktu itu hujan, dan semua orang sedang menunggu KRL.

examples.en: Rina was late because she had missed the first bus.
examples.id: Rina terlambat karena dia sudah ketinggalan bus pertama.

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the beach and I saw a turtle.
examples.id: Kemarin saya pergi ke pantai dan saya melihat penyu.

id.title: Tiga past tense dalam satu cerita
id.explanation: Past continuous (was/were + -ing) adalah latarnya: apa yang sedang terjadi. Past simple menceritakan kejadian-kejadiannya, berurutan. Past perfect (had + bentuk ketiga) kembali ke sesuatu yang terjadi lebih dulu. Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak berubah, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris setiap kata kerja dalam cerita lampau memakai bentuk lampau: Yesterday I went to the beach and I saw a turtle (bukan 'I go … I see').

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with in the end or at the end of: Everyone clapped ___ the film.
guidedPractice.hint: A noun (the film) comes after the gap: you need 'of'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'walk': I ___ to the KRL station when it started to rain.
guidedPractice.hint: The walk is the background, already happening when the rain started: was/were + -ing.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Last weekend I go to the market and I buy some mangoes.
expected: last weekend i went to the market and i bought some mangoes
last weekend i went to the market and bought some mangoes
i went to the market last weekend and i bought some mangoes
i went to the market last weekend and bought some mangoes
guidedPractice.hint: It's a past story: both verbs change (go → went, buy → bought).

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with embarrassing or embarrassed: I called my new boss by the wrong name. I was so ___!
guidedPractice.hint: How did you feel? -ed is for how a person feels.

guidedPractice.prompt: Your friend says: 'I fell asleep on the KRL and woke up in Bogor!' React in 2–4 words.
guidedPractice.hint: Show surprise, or ask for the rest of the story.

independentPractice.prompt: Tell a short story (4–5 sentences) about a trip, for example mudik. Set the scene first, then use Suddenly and In the end.
independentPractice.hint: Scene (when, where, what was happening) → what happened → how it ended.

independentPractice.prompt: Tell a short story about a funny or embarrassing moment: set the scene (was/were + -ing), say what happened (past simple), and go back to one earlier event (had + third form).
independentPractice.hint: Example: I was standing at the bus stop. Suddenly I realised I had put my shirt on inside out!

independentPractice.prompt: Finish this story with Luckily or Unfortunately and one more sentence: I left my phone in the ojek.
independentPractice.hint: Luckily = something good happened next; Unfortunately = something bad.

assessment.prompt: Complete the story with one word that means 'quickly, and nobody expected it': We were sitting in the garden at my sister's wedding. ___ it started to rain heavily, and everyone ran inside.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Suddenly (tiba-tiba). Also accept 'All of a sudden'. 'Then' = 40 (correct English but not the word described). 'Finally', 'In the end' = 0 (they introduce the end, not a surprise).

assessment.prompt: Complete with In the end or At the end of: The mudik traffic was terrible, and our bus didn't come for three hours. We looked for another bus, but they were all full. ___, we went back home and travelled the next day.
assessment.rubric: Correct: In the end (the final result after the problems). 'At the end of' = 0 (it needs a noun after it: at the end of the day). 'Finally' = 60 (natural, but not one of the two choices). 'In the end of' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'sleep': It was 2 a.m. on the night bus to Surabaya. Most of the passengers ___ when the bus suddenly stopped.
assessment.rubric: Correct: were sleeping (the background, already in progress when the bus stopped). 'was sleeping' = 60 (right tense, but passengers = they → were). 'slept' = 30. 'had slept' or 'sleep' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'go': Pak Hasan's train was very late. When he got to the meeting, the clients ___ home, so he had to send them the report by email.
assessment.rubric: Correct: had gone (they went home earlier, before he arrived). 'had went' = 50 (right idea, wrong third form). 'went' = 30 (means they left at the moment he arrived). 'were going' = 20. 'go' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'see': Yesterday we went to Ancol with the kids, and we ___ a dolphin show.
assessment.rubric: Correct: saw (a past story: every verb changes, not just the first). 'see' = 0 (the Indonesian no-tense trap). 'seed' = 20. 'were seeing' or 'had seen' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Listen to your friend's story. It isn't finished yet. Write a short reaction (2–5 words) that asks to hear the rest.
assessment.listen: So I was standing on the stage at my cousin's wedding, with the microphone in my hand. I looked down at my shoes, and then I saw something terrible.
acceptableAnswers: oh no what did you see
assessment.rubric: Correct: any short question or phrase that asks for the rest (What happened next? / What did you see? / And then what?). A reaction plus a question (Oh no! What happened?) is full marks. Only 'Really?' or 'No way!' = 60 (a good reaction, but it doesn't ask for more). 'That's great!' or 'Lucky you!' = 0 (wrong mood).

assessment.prompt: Complete with Luckily or Unfortunately: I left my phone on the KRL. ___, a woman found it and gave it to the station staff, so I got it back the same day.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Luckily (= Fortunately, untungnya): what follows is good news. 'Unfortunately' = 0 (that's for bad news). 'Lucky' = 50 (right idea, but it needs -ly here).

blocks.text:
When you tell a friend about something that happened (a funny moment, a scary night, a trip, a problem at work), the story is easy to follow if it has **three parts**:
- **Set the scene**: when, where, who, and what was happening. *Last Friday I was on the KRL to Bogor. It was packed.*
- **What happened**: the events, one after another. *Suddenly the train stopped between two stations…*
- **How it ended and how you felt**: *In the end, we got to Bogor an hour late. I was so tired!*

Start with a **time** (*Last Lebaran…, Yesterday…, A few years ago…*) so your listener knows it's a past story. A friendly way to begin: *Did I tell you about my cousin's wedding?*

id.text:
Saat kamu bercerita ke teman tentang sesuatu yang terjadi (momen lucu, malam yang menyeramkan, perjalanan, masalah di kantor), ceritanya mudah diikuti kalau punya **tiga bagian**:
- **Bangun latarnya**: kapan, di mana, siapa, dan apa yang sedang terjadi. *Last Friday I was on the KRL to Bogor. It was packed.*
- **Apa yang terjadi**: kejadian-kejadiannya, satu per satu. *Suddenly the train stopped between two stations…*
- **Bagaimana akhirnya dan apa yang kamu rasakan**: *In the end, we got to Bogor an hour late. I was so tired!*

Mulai dengan **keterangan waktu** (*Last Lebaran…, Yesterday…, A few years ago…*) supaya pendengarmu tahu ini cerita masa lalu. Cara ramah untuk memulai: *Did I tell you about my cousin's wedding?* (Aku sudah cerita belum soal nikahan sepupuku?)

rows.en: It was my cousin's wedding in Bandung, and the hall was full of guests.
rows.id: Waktu itu nikahan sepupuku di Bandung, dan gedungnya penuh tamu.

rows.en: I was carrying a big plate of food to my table.
rows.id: Aku sedang membawa sepiring besar makanan ke mejaku.

rows.en: Suddenly I slipped, and the food went everywhere.
rows.id: Tiba-tiba aku terpeleset, dan makanannya tumpah ke mana-mana.

rows.en: Everyone was looking at me. It was so embarrassing!
rows.id: Semua orang melihat ke arahku. Malu banget!

rows.en: In the end, the bride laughed and helped me, so I felt better.
rows.id: Akhirnya, pengantin wanitanya tertawa dan membantuku, jadi aku merasa lebih baik.
rows.note: how it ended + how I felt

blocks.text: Keep the scene **short** (one or two sentences), then move to the events: listeners want to know what happened. And don't stop without an ending, or your friend will ask: *So what happened in the end?*

id.text: Buat latarnya **singkat** (satu atau dua kalimat), lalu masuk ke kejadiannya: pendengar ingin tahu apa yang terjadi. Dan jangan berhenti tanpa akhir, nanti temanmu bertanya: *So what happened in the end?* (Terus akhirnya gimana?)

options: In the end, we got home at 2 a.m.
It was a rainy night, and we were waiting for a taxi outside the mall.
Suddenly a car stopped next to us.
blocks.explain: The scene tells when, where and what was happening (were waiting). 'Suddenly a car stopped' is an event, and 'In the end…' is how the story ended.

id.explain: Latar menceritakan kapan, di mana dan apa yang sedang terjadi (were waiting). 'Suddenly a car stopped' adalah kejadian, dan 'In the end…' adalah akhir ceritanya.

blocks.text:
From A2 you know **first, then, next, after that** and **finally** for events in order. Stories need three more:
- **suddenly** (*tiba-tiba*): something quick that nobody expected. It often cuts into the background: *We were having dinner. **Suddenly** the lights went out.*
- **in the end** (*akhirnya, pada akhirnya*): the final result, after problems or changes. *We looked for a taxi for an hour. **In the end**, we took the KRL.*
- **at the end of** + a thing or a time (*di akhir*): *at the end of the film, at the end of the day, at the end of the month*.

**finally** also means *akhirnya*, especially after a long wait: *We waited for two hours. **Finally**, the bus came.* In many stories, **finally** and **in the end** both work for the last event.

id.text:
Dari A2 kamu sudah tahu **first, then, next, after that** dan **finally** untuk kejadian yang berurutan. Cerita butuh tiga lagi:
- **suddenly** (*tiba-tiba*): sesuatu yang cepat dan tidak ada yang menduga. Sering memotong latarnya: *We were having dinner. **Suddenly** the lights went out.*
- **in the end** (*akhirnya, pada akhirnya*): hasil akhirnya, setelah ada masalah atau perubahan. *We looked for a taxi for an hour. **In the end**, we took the KRL.*
- **at the end of** + benda atau waktu (*di akhir*): *at the end of the film, at the end of the day, at the end of the month*.

**finally** juga berarti *akhirnya*, terutama setelah menunggu lama: *We waited for two hours. **Finally**, the bus came.* Di banyak cerita, **finally** dan **in the end** sama-sama bisa dipakai untuk kejadian terakhir.

rows.en: First, we bought our train tickets online.
rows.id: Pertama-tama, kami membeli tiket kereta secara online.

rows.en: After that, we packed our bags.
rows.id: Setelah itu, kami mengemas tas.

rows.en: Suddenly my phone rang: there was a problem with our train!
rows.id: Tiba-tiba HP-ku berbunyi: ada masalah dengan kereta kami!

rows.en: In the end, we went by bus.
rows.id: Akhirnya, kami pergi naik bus.
rows.note: the final result, after the problem

rows.en: At the end of the trip, we were tired but happy.
rows.id: Di akhir perjalanan, kami capek tapi senang.
rows.note: at the end of + a noun

id.note: at the end of + kata benda

blocks.text:
**in the end** vs **at the end of**: *In the end of the film, …* ✗ → *At the end of the film, …* ✓. **in the end** has no *of* and no noun after it: it means 'after everything'. (You'll also hear *at the end* alone when it's clear what ended: *Everyone clapped at the end.* That's correct too.)
And remember from A2: when Indonesian *akhirnya* means a **result**, English uses **so**: *Hujan, akhirnya kami di rumah* → *It rained, **so** we stayed home.*

id.text:
**in the end** vs **at the end of**: *In the end of the film, …* ✗ → *At the end of the film, …* ✓. **in the end** tidak memakai *of* dan tidak diikuti kata benda: artinya 'setelah semuanya'. (Kamu juga akan mendengar *at the end* saja kalau sudah jelas apa yang berakhir: *Everyone clapped at the end.* Itu juga benar.)
Dan ingat dari A2: kalau *akhirnya* dalam bahasa Indonesia berarti **akibat**, bahasa Inggris memakai **so**: *Hujan, akhirnya kami di rumah* → *It rained, **so** we stayed home.*

blocks.prompt: Our team had a small party ___ the year.
blocks.explain: A noun (the year) comes next, so use at the end of (di akhir tahun). 'in the end of' is a common mistake, and 'in the end' can't have a noun after it.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Our team had a small party ___ the year.
id.explain: Setelahnya ada kata benda (the year), jadi pakai at the end of (di akhir tahun). 'in the end of' adalah kesalahan yang umum, dan 'in the end' tidak bisa diikuti kata benda.

blocks.text:
You know all three tenses from earlier lessons. In a story, each one has a **job**:
- **Past continuous** (was/were + -ing) = the **background**, what was already happening: *It was raining. People were waiting for the KRL.*
- **Past simple** = the **events**, the main line of the story, in order: *The train came. Everyone pushed in.*
- **Past perfect** (had + third form) = going **back** to something that happened **earlier**: *I couldn't tap in because I had left my card at home.*

Three questions help: **What was happening?** (was/were + -ing) **What happened?** (past simple) **What had happened before?** (had + third form). Most of a story is past simple: the other two are for the scene and for going back.

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu ketiga tense ini dari pelajaran sebelumnya. Dalam cerita, masing-masing punya **tugas**:
- **Past continuous** (was/were + -ing) = **latar**, apa yang sedang terjadi: *It was raining. People were waiting for the KRL.*
- **Past simple** = **kejadian-kejadiannya**, alur utama cerita, berurutan: *The train came. Everyone pushed in.*
- **Past perfect** (had + bentuk ketiga) = **kembali** ke sesuatu yang terjadi **lebih dulu**: *I couldn't tap in because I had left my card at home.* (Aku nggak bisa tap masuk karena kartuku ketinggalan di rumah.)

Tiga pertanyaan ini membantu: **What was happening?** (apa yang sedang terjadi → was/were + -ing) **What happened?** (apa yang terjadi → past simple) **What had happened before?** (apa yang sudah terjadi sebelumnya → had + bentuk ketiga). Sebagian besar cerita memakai past simple: dua yang lain untuk latar dan untuk kembali ke masa sebelumnya.

rows.en: It was Monday morning, and the KRL to Jakarta was packed.
rows.id: Senin pagi itu, KRL ke Jakarta penuh sesak.

rows.en: I was standing near the door, and everyone was looking at their phones.
rows.id: Aku sedang berdiri dekat pintu, dan semua orang sedang melihat HP mereka.

rows.en: Suddenly the train stopped between two stations.
rows.id: Tiba-tiba keretanya berhenti di antara dua stasiun.

rows.en: I wanted to call my boss, but my phone had died.
rows.id: Aku mau menelepon bosku, tapi HP-ku sudah mati (baterainya habis).
rows.note: earlier → had + third form (die → died → died)

id.note: lebih dulu → had + bentuk ketiga (die → died → died)

rows.en: In the end, I got to the office forty minutes late.
rows.id: Akhirnya, aku sampai di kantor terlambat empat puluh menit.

blocks.text:
**Indonesian trap: no tense marking.** Indonesian verbs don't change: the time word does the work (*Kemarin saya pergi ke pantai dan saya lihat penyu*). English changes **every** verb in a past story: *Yesterday I go to the beach and I see a turtle* ✗ → *Yesterday I **went** to the beach and I **saw** a turtle* ✓. Check the second and third verbs too, not just the first.
Two more slips: don't put every verb in -ing (that's a scene with no events), and don't use **had** for a single event (*Last week I had gone to Bogor* ✗ → *Last week I **went** to Bogor* ✓).

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: tidak ada penanda waktu pada kata kerja.** Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak berubah: kata keterangan waktunya yang bekerja (*Kemarin saya pergi ke pantai dan saya lihat penyu*). Bahasa Inggris mengubah **setiap** kata kerja dalam cerita lampau: *Yesterday I go to the beach and I see a turtle* ✗ → *Yesterday I **went** to the beach and I **saw** a turtle* ✓. Periksa juga kata kerja kedua dan ketiga, bukan hanya yang pertama.
Dua kesalahan lain: jangan pakai -ing untuk semua kata kerja (itu latar tanpa kejadian), dan jangan pakai **had** untuk satu kejadian saja (*Last week I had gone to Bogor* ✗ → *Last week I **went** to Bogor* ✓).

blocks.prompt: It was 6 p.m., and I ___ home on an ojek when it started to rain.
blocks.explain: The ride is the background, already happening when the rain started → was riding. 'had ridden' would mean the ride was finished before the rain, and 'ride' is the Indonesian no-tense trap.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: It was 6 p.m., and I ___ home on an ojek when it started to rain.
id.explain: Naik ojeknya adalah latar, sedang berlangsung saat hujan mulai → was riding. 'had ridden' berarti perjalanannya sudah selesai sebelum hujan, dan 'ride' adalah jebakan tanpa tense dari bahasa Indonesia.

blocks.text:
A list of events is boring. Bring your story to life with:
- **details**: who, where, what you saw or heard. *There were 500 guests. The music was really loud.*
- **feelings** inside the story: *I couldn't believe it!* (aku nggak percaya!) *It was so embarrassing!* *I was so scared.* *We laughed so much.* (**so** here = very, like *so hot*.)
- **Luckily, …** (*untungnya*) before something good, and **Unfortunately, …** (*sayangnya*) before something bad: *Unfortunately, it started to rain. Luckily, I had an umbrella.* (**Fortunately** = luckily.)

id.text:
Daftar kejadian saja itu membosankan. Hidupkan ceritamu dengan:
- **detail**: siapa, di mana, apa yang kamu lihat atau dengar. *There were 500 guests. The music was really loud.*
- **perasaan** di dalam cerita: *I couldn't believe it!* (aku nggak percaya!) *It was so embarrassing!* (malu banget!) *I was so scared.* (aku takut banget.) *We laughed so much.* (kami tertawa terus.) (**so** di sini = sangat, seperti *so hot*.)
- **Luckily, …** (*untungnya*) sebelum hal yang baik, dan **Unfortunately, …** (*sayangnya*) sebelum hal yang buruk: *Unfortunately, it started to rain. Luckily, I had an umbrella.* (**Fortunately** = luckily.)

rows.en: The KRL was packed, and it was really hot.
rows.id: KRL-nya penuh sesak, dan panas sekali.

rows.en: I couldn't believe it! The man next to me was my old teacher.
rows.id: Aku nggak percaya! Laki-laki di sebelahku ternyata guru lamaku.

rows.en: Unfortunately, the last bus had already left.
rows.id: Sayangnya, bus terakhir sudah berangkat.

rows.en: Luckily, a kind ojek driver took us home.
rows.id: Untungnya, seorang pengemudi ojek yang baik mengantar kami pulang.

rows.en: It was a scary night, and I was really scared.
rows.id: Malam itu menyeramkan, dan aku benar-benar takut.

blocks.text: **-ing or -ed?** The **-ing** word describes the situation (*embarrassing* = memalukan); the **-ed** word describes how a person feels (*embarrassed* = malu). *It was so embarrassing* ✓, *I was so embarrassed* ✓, but *I was so embarrassing* ✗ means 'saya sangat memalukan' (you made other people feel bad!). The same works for **boring / bored, tiring / tired, surprising / surprised**. One pair is different: **scary** (menyeramkan) / **scared** (takut).

id.text: **-ing atau -ed?** Kata **-ing** menggambarkan situasinya (*embarrassing* = memalukan); kata **-ed** menggambarkan perasaan seseorang (*embarrassed* = malu). *It was so embarrassing* ✓, *I was so embarrassed* ✓, tapi *I was so embarrassing* ✗ artinya 'saya sangat memalukan' (kamu yang membuat orang lain malu!). Begitu juga **boring / bored, tiring / tired, surprising / surprised**. Ada satu pasangan yang berbeda: **scary** (menyeramkan) / **scared** (takut).

blocks.prompt: The film was so long. I was so ___ that I fell asleep.
blocks.explain: How did I feel? → bored (bosan). 'I was so boring' would mean I made other people bored. The film was boring.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The film was so long. I was so ___ that I fell asleep.
id.explain: Apa yang kurasakan? → bored (bosan). 'I was so boring' berarti aku yang membuat orang lain bosan. Filmnya yang boring (membosankan).

blocks.text:
A story is a conversation. When a friend tells you a story, react, so they know you're listening and want more:
- **surprise**: *Really?* / *No way!* / *Seriously?* (masa sih? / yang bener!)
- **asking for more**: *What happened next?* / *And then what?* / *How did that happen?* (kok bisa?)
- **bad news**: *Oh no!* / *That's terrible!* / *Poor you!* (kasihan)
- **funny or embarrassing**: *How embarrassing!* / *That's so funny!*
- **a good ending**: *Thank goodness!* / *Lucky you!*

Choose a reaction that matches the **mood** of the story: don't say *That's great!* to bad news.

id.text:
Cerita itu percakapan. Saat temanmu bercerita, beri reaksi, supaya dia tahu kamu mendengarkan dan ingin tahu lanjutannya:
- **kaget**: *Really?* / *No way!* / *Seriously?* (masa sih? / yang bener!)
- **minta lanjutannya**: *What happened next?* / *And then what?* (terus gimana?) / *How did that happen?* (kok bisa?)
- **kabar buruk**: *Oh no!* / *That's terrible!* / *Poor you!* (kasihan)
- **lucu atau memalukan**: *How embarrassing!* (malu banget!) / *That's so funny!* (lucu banget!)
- **akhir yang baik**: *Thank goodness!* (syukurlah!) / *Lucky you!* (beruntung banget kamu!)

Pilih reaksi yang cocok dengan **suasana** ceritanya: jangan bilang *That's great!* untuk kabar buruk.

rows.en: I met my favourite singer at the airport! — No way! Did you take a photo?
rows.id: Aku ketemu penyanyi favoritku di bandara! — Masa sih! Kamu foto bareng?

rows.en: Someone took my helmet at the mall. — Oh no! Poor you!
rows.id: Helmku diambil orang di mal. — Aduh! Kasihan!

rows.en: My train was two hours late. — Really? How did that happen?
rows.id: Keretaku terlambat dua jam. — Masa? Kok bisa?

rows.en: And then I sang in front of my boss. — How embarrassing!
rows.id: Terus aku menyanyi di depan bosku. — Malu banget!

blocks.text: Don't translate word by word: *kasihan* → **Poor you!** (not 'Pity you'); *kok bisa?* → **How did that happen?**; *masa sih?* → **Really?** or **No way!** Here **No way!** is friendly surprise, not 'tidak mau'. *favourite* is British; Americans write *favorite*.

id.text: Jangan terjemahkan kata per kata: *kasihan* → **Poor you!** (bukan 'Pity you'); *kok bisa?* → **How did that happen?**; *masa sih?* → **Really?** atau **No way!** Di sini **No way!** artinya kaget dengan ramah, bukan 'tidak mau'. *favourite* adalah ejaan Inggris British; orang Amerika menulis *favorite*.

blocks.prompt: Your friend says: 'My boss shouted at me in front of everyone today.' Which reaction fits best?
blocks.explain: It's bad news, so react with sympathy: Oh no! That's terrible. 'Lucky you!' is for good news, and laughing at it would be rude.

id.prompt: Temanmu bilang: 'My boss shouted at me in front of everyone today.' Reaksi mana yang paling cocok?
id.explain: Itu kabar buruk, jadi tunjukkan simpati: Oh no! That's terrible. 'Lucky you!' untuk kabar baik, dan menertawakannya tidak sopan.

resources.title: How to Tell a Story in English - Using Past Tense
resources.note: A video lesson, all in English, on building a story step by step: set the scene, the problem, and how it ended. It's a little above this lesson's level in places, and its example stories use a few extra forms (such as had been + -ing) that you don't need yet.

id.note: Video pelajaran, seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris, tentang menyusun cerita langkah demi langkah: membangun latar, masalahnya, dan bagaimana akhirnya. Di beberapa bagian sedikit di atas level pelajaran ini, dan contoh ceritanya memakai beberapa bentuk tambahan (seperti had been + -ing) yang belum perlu kamu pelajari.

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi! Kamu sudah tahu past simple, past continuous dan past perfect. Sekarang kamu akan memakainya bersama untuk bercerita sungguhan: membangun latar, menceritakan apa yang terjadi secara berurutan, menambahkan perasaanmu, dan memberi reaksi saat temanmu bercerita. Pemanasan: ingat-ingat satu momen lucu, menyeramkan atau memalukan yang pernah kamu alami.
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya 'in the end' dan 'at the end of'?
Bagaimana saya tahu past tense mana yang dipakai dalam cerita?
Apa yang bisa saya katakan saat teman bercerita?

assessment.ts-1: Lengkapi ceritanya dengan satu kata yang artinya 'cepat, dan tidak ada yang menduga': We were sitting in the garden at my sister's wedding. ___ it started to rain heavily, and everyone ran inside.
assessment.ts-2: Lengkapi dengan In the end atau At the end of: The mudik traffic was terrible, and our bus didn't come for three hours. We looked for another bus, but they were all full. ___, we went back home and travelled the next day.
assessment.ts-3: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'sleep': It was 2 a.m. on the night bus to Surabaya. Most of the passengers ___ when the bus suddenly stopped.
assessment.ts-4: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'go': Pak Hasan's train was very late. When he got to the meeting, the clients ___ home, so he had to send them the report by email.
assessment.ts-5: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'see': Yesterday we went to Ancol with the kids, and we ___ a dolphin show.
assessment.ts-6: Dengarkan cerita temanmu. Ceritanya belum selesai. Tulis reaksi singkat (2–5 kata) dalam bahasa Inggris untuk meminta lanjutan ceritanya.
assessment.ts-7: Lengkapi dengan Luckily atau Unfortunately: I left my phone on the KRL. ___, a woman found it and gave it to the station staff, so I got it back the same day.
